title: Introduction to computer vision
description: Choose an image task and build an evaluation that reflects real use.
objectives: Design a transfer-learning baseline without image leakage
explanation: Computer vision transforms images into outputs for a task. Classification assigns labels to an image. Detection adds object locations, usually boxes. Segmentation assigns labels to pixels. Choose the output required by the user before selecting a model or collecting annotations.

Transfer learning starts with a model trained elsewhere. You can freeze a feature extractor and train a new head, or fine-tune selected layers. Keep resize, channel order, and normalization consistent with the chosen model. Apply random augmentation to training images, while evaluation preprocessing should be repeatable.

Split by the source of correlated images. Adjacent video frames, repeated photos of the same object, or one camera session can leak across a random split. Evaluate lighting, viewpoint, background, and device differences. A model can exploit a label watermark instead of learning the intended object.

terms.definition: Assigning a category to individual pixels.
Adapting representations learned from another training task.

example: A fictional packaging inspection project needs the location of torn labels, so image-level classification alone is insufficient. Keep all photos of a package in one partition and include a separate lighting setup in the evaluation.
mistakes: Changing image normalization between training and inference.
Treating a confidence score as a calibrated probability without checking.
exercise: Define an inspection task with five invented image descriptions. Choose the annotation type, group-based split, two realistic augmentations, and a failure review plan. Explain what image-level accuracy would miss.

questions.question: Which output distinguishes detection from image classification?
questions.answer: Detection includes object locations as well as category predictions.
questions.distractor: Detection only reports the file size.

questions.question: What should match a pretrained vision model at inference?
questions.answer: The expected input channels, size handling, and normalization.
questions.distractor: Any arbitrary preprocessing because pretrained models are invariant to it.

questions.question: Why keep photos of one physical object in one data split?
questions.answer: Closely related images can otherwise make evaluation unrealistically easy.
questions.distractor: Objects cannot be photographed more than once.

questions.question: How does a frozen feature extractor differ from full fine-tuning?
questions.answer: Its parameters stay fixed while a task-specific head can be trained.
questions.distractor: It retrains every parameter from random values.

questions.question: What is a useful robustness check for a camera classifier?
questions.answer: Evaluate different lighting and backgrounds representative of deployment.
questions.distractor: Only repeat the same image many times.
